name: Succinyl-CoA synthetase deficiency
aliases: mtDNA depletion syndrome with methylmalonic aciduria

clinicalPearls: A deficiency of the tricarboxylic-acid-cycle enzyme succinyl-CoA synthetase (succinate-CoA ligase) arising from variants in SUCLA2 (a beta subunit) or SUCLG1 (the alpha subunit); it behaves as a mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome.

SUCLA2 disease is an encephalomyopathic mtDNA depletion syndrome that typically begins in infancy with hypotonia, muscle atrophy, dystonia or another movement disorder, sensorineural hearing loss and feeding difficulty.

SUCLG1 disease tends to be more severe and earlier in onset — the alpha subunit is shared by both the ATP- and GTP-forming isoenzymes — often with fatal neonatal lactic acidosis and sometimes hepatic involvement.

A characteristic biochemical clue is mild-to-moderate methylmalonic aciduria with raised methylcitrate, plus elevated succinylcarnitine (a C4-dicarboxylylcarnitine) on the acylcarnitine profile, which helps separate it from classical methylmalonic acidaemia.
Lactic acidosis and Leigh-like basal ganglia signal change on MRI are common findings.
Depletion of mitochondrial DNA is demonstrable in skeletal muscle.
The methylmalonic aciduria is not cobalamin-responsive, distinguishing it from vitamin B12 (cobalamin) metabolic disorders.
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary; no curative therapy is available.
reference.pathophysiology: Succinyl-CoA synthetase (succinate-CoA ligase) is a tricarboxylic-acid-cycle enzyme that reversibly converts succinyl-CoA to succinate with substrate-level phosphorylation of ADP or GDP. Its alpha subunit, encoded by SUCLG1, partners either with the ATP-forming beta subunit encoded by SUCLA2 or with the GTP-forming beta subunit encoded by SUCLG2, so loss of the shared alpha subunit tends to be more severe than loss of a single beta subunit. The enzyme associates with mitochondrial nucleoside diphosphate kinase to maintain the matrix nucleotide pool needed for mtDNA replication, and deficiency therefore causes mitochondrial DNA depletion with multiple respiratory-chain enzyme deficiencies. Reduced succinyl-CoA turnover shifts the methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA equilibrium, producing the characteristic mild methylmalonic aciduria, raised methylcitrate and elevated succinylcarnitine. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Classical methylmalonic acidaemia (MUT and cobalamin defects) — with much higher methylmalonic acid and cobalamin-responsive forms
Other mtDNA depletion syndromes (POLG, DGUOK, MPV17, TK2, RRM2B)
Leigh syndrome of other genetic cause
Primary lactic acidosis of other mitochondrial aetiology
The sibling genotype (SUCLA2 versus SUCLG1), which differ in severity and organ involvement
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids showing mild methylmalonic aciduria and raised methylcitrate
Brain MRI for basal ganglia and Leigh-like changes
Muscle biopsy with mtDNA quantification and respiratory-chain enzymology
SUCLA2 and SUCLG1 sequencing or a mitochondrial gene panel
Audiological assessment for sensorineural hearing loss
redFlags: Neonatal lactic acidosis with rapid deterioration, which favours SUCLG1 disease
Progressive dystonia, hypotonia and loss of milestones in infancy
New or evolving basal ganglia signal change on MRI
Sensorineural hearing loss accompanying a movement disorder
reference.prognosis: The condition is serious: SUCLG1 disease is frequently fatal in the neonatal period or infancy, whereas SUCLA2 disease often allows survival into childhood or beyond, albeit with significant disability.
pitfalls: Misreading the mild methylmalonic aciduria as classical methylmalonic acidaemia and giving cobalamin, which is ineffective here.
Missing the diagnosis when the acylcarnitine profile, and specifically succinylcarnitine, is not scrutinised.
Attributing the lactic acidosis solely to acute intercurrent illness.
Failing to quantify mitochondrial DNA in muscle when a depletion syndrome is suspected.
management: Provide supportive mitochondrial care, as no disease-modifying therapy exists for this mtDNA depletion syndrome
Manage lactic acidosis with fluids and buffering during metabolic decompensation and minimise catabolic stress
Ensure nutritional support with nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding for feeding difficulty and poor growth
Treat dystonia and movement disorder with appropriate agents alongside physiotherapy, occupational and speech therapy
Rehabilitate sensorineural hearing loss with hearing aids or cochlear implantation
Avoid mitochondrial toxins such as sodium valproate and aminoglycosides, and a cofactor supplement regimen may be trialled
Offer genetic counselling and family testing for autosomal recessive SUCLA2 or SUCLG1 variants, with monitoring of development, hearing and neuroimaging
Coordinate multidisciplinary care through metabolic and mitochondrial medicine specialists
